title: Coherent optical control of a thousand qubits in a three-dimensional trapped-ion crystal
authors: Yue Li, Yuxiang Huang, Yi Li, Xu Cheng, Zihan Xie, Qingyuan Mei, Chang-Ling Zou, Ya Wang, Xinhua Peng, Yiheng Lin, Jiangfeng Du
abstract: Leading quantum platforms are largely limited to one or two dimensions, whereas three-dimensional Coulomb crystals of trapped ions self-assemble into dense qubit arrays with no rearrangement overhead. Coherent optical control of such crystals has nonetheless been out of reach, because the optical transition couples to nearly all $3N$ collective modes, i.e., a thermally occupied quasi-continuum bath. Here we cool about 3,600 modes of a crystal of over 1,200 ions below single-phonon occupation, using a continuous cooling band that spans more than five octaves in vibrational spectrum, from about 50 kHz to 2.1 MHz. The crystal then serves as a register of optical qubits, allowing global initialization, coherent manipulation and collective detection. We demonstrate ensemble optical coherence of 21.6 milliseconds and reduce the optical-transition frequency uncertainty from 389 Hz for a single ion to 12 Hz for over a thousand ions, approaching the expected projection-noise scaling. Our approach could be extended to even larger crystals with phonon-mediated many-body couplings, opening a route towards entanglement-enhanced precision metrology and three-dimensional quantum simulation, particularly with spatial-shaped illumination for region-resolved collective control.
summary: This paper reports on the coherent optical control of a large, three-dimensional crystal of trapped ions. The key challenge—the coupling to a dense spectrum of vibrational modes—is overcome by using broadband cooling techniques. The results confirm that the crystal functions as a high-fidelity quantum register, achieving long coherence times and superior frequency precision scaling with ion number.
main_problem: Achieving coherent optical control and high-precision metrology in large, three-dimensional (3D) trapped-ion crystals, which is challenging due to the coupling of the optical transition to a quasi-continuum bath of collective vibrational modes.
main_result: The authors successfully cooled thousands of vibrational modes below the single-phonon occupation and demonstrated ensemble optical coherence of 21.6 ms, showing that the dense mode spectrum does not impede global coherent control.
method: The experiment utilizes broadband cooling via parallel-EIT techniques, followed by coherent manipulation measurements like Rabi oscillations and Ramsey interferometry on the trapped ion ensemble.
model_or_system: The physical system is a 3D Coulomb crystal of over 1,200 trapped ions. The complexity arises from the dense, quasi-continuous spectrum of $\approx 3,600$ normal modes, which must be addressed for global control.
key_observables: Ensemble optical coherence time ($T_2$), optical-transition frequency uncertainty ($\sigma/2\pi$), mean phonon occupation ($ ar{n}$), and local Rabi frequencies.
important_parameters: Ion number ($N_{	ext{ion}} \approx 1,265$), cooling bandwidth (50 kHz to 2.1 MHz), and frequency uncertainty scaling approaching projection-noise limits.
main_assumptions: The cooling method relies on creating multiple cooling windows via parallel resonances to achieve broadband, sub-Doppler cooling without resolving individual modes.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the experimental setup, the dense vibrational spectrum, the broadband cooling process via sideband asymmetry comparison, and the scaling of frequency uncertainty with ion number.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the feasibility of cooling the dense mode spectrum, then demonstrating global coherent control (Rabi oscillations), and finally quantifying the metrological improvement by showing frequency uncertainty scaling towards the standard quantum limit.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the scaling challenge in trapped-ion quantum computing platforms by demonstrating robust global control despite the presence of a complex, high-dimensional vibrational bath, which is a major bottleneck in scaling trapped-ion quantum processors.
